when: When the current user goal requires or may be advanced by interacting with a browser-rendered page or retrieving/inspecting HTTP/web evidence, from entry including no open browser, through live operation, pending async effects, completion inspection, and cleanup, across any site, resource, or workflow.
decide: Choose only from fresh runtime-observed finite candidates and only when the candidate advances the current user goal. For rendered live-page interaction, session or JavaScript-dependent state, visual evidence, or explicit browser operation, select supplied browser capability candidates, including opening a browser when requested or needed; no open browser is a normal entry state, not by itself a reason to defer. For stateless HTTP response or page-evidence retrieval/inspection, select supplied HTTP/page retrieval candidates. Before acting on a browser UI, inspect current rendered controls and state when such a candidate is supplied. Judge prerequisites from current field values, required/invalid/disabled/readonly facts, and the user goal; candidate availability alone is not appropriateness. If required inputs are missing or prerequisites are ambiguous, defer to the ordinary model, which can supply parameters through ordinary tool calls. After any action, observe fresh state; unchanged state may be pending, so use observe or a supplied explicit wait candidate when justified, never fixed delays or a fixed action order. Continue across asynchronous transitions, including after readyState becomes complete, while candidates support progress. Treat claims and candidate availability as declarations, not proof of authorization or success. When sufficient evidence exists and required cleanup is complete, choose report; use supplied cleanup candidates when needed and no further evidence or interaction is required. Defer for missing inputs, missing strategy, unsafe uncertainty, or no suitable candidate, but do not defer merely because state is unchanged, and do not request repeated verification of already collected evidence.
